sections.content:
So the last RIGHT action added 2 white pixels and 2 gray pixels, while removing 4 charcoal pixels. This means the track extended by 2 pixels (one white block and one gray block, each 2x2=4 pixels, but only 2 new pixels of each). Wait, that doesn't add up. Let me think again.
Actually, looking at the track pattern, it alternates between white (w) and gray (g) blocks. Each block is 2x2=4 pixels. The track has 8 white blocks (40 pixels) and some gray blocks (102 pixels before, 104 after).
The diff shows w: +2, g: +2, c: -4. So 2 white + 2 gray pixels were added, replacing 4 charcoal pixels. This means one new 2x2 block was added to the track (2 white + 2 gray = 4 pixels total, but they come from different colors).
Wait, that's only 4 pixels total added (2w + 2g), replacing 4 charcoal pixels. So the track extended by one position.
Let me try pressing RIGHT again to see if the track continues to extend.

w_blocks.sort()

# Check colored blocks
for n in seg:
    if n['color'] in ['R', 'b', 'N'] and n['pixels'] == 16:
        b = n['boundary']
        minr = min(p[0] for p in b)
        minc = min(p[1] for p in b)
        print("color=%s, bounds=(%d,%d)-..." % (n['color'], minr, minc))
